findings.text: forEach now calls syncHandlerEntries, which reads handlers.length. Before this change utils.forEach tolerated a null or undefined handlers value. If code sets `manager.handlers = null`, forEach, use and eject now throw a TypeError.

Entry bookkeeping assumes indexes only change through this class. If external code splices or reorders `manager.handlers` without changing its length, handlers[entry.index] points at a different handler. eject(id) then silently skips the removal, so the interceptor stays active.

1.reason: Because syncHandlerEntries only resynchronizes entries on a reference change or length change, a length-preserving external reorder leaves stale index mappings, causing eject to treat the moved handler as invalidated and skip removal.
